title: Context chunking experiments and quicknotes
body:
Quick purpose: capture early intuition and experiment ideas for splitting long contexts into stable fragments + rerank/cross-attend strategies so we can hit <200ms P95 on customer conversational workloads while keeping recall of earlier content. Not polished; brain dump for Arjun/Maya pairing next week.

Top-level idea:
- Many customer chats contain intermittently relevant past passages (policy snippets, previous messages, doc excerpts). We can treat the long context as a time-ordered stream of fragments and (cheaply) select a subset to materialize into KV-shard for the current turn.
- Two axes: selection (which fragments to keep) and composition (how to stitch them so model sees them efficiently).

Notes from paper skim (fast takeaways):
- Paper A (dense fragment rerank, arXiv:2306.16560): good baseline for unsupervised chunk scoring via TF-IDF + lightweight bi-encoder. Their eval shows small loss when selecting top-K fragments vs full context for retrieval tasks. Potential pivot: use lightweight encoder that runs on CPU and pushes selected fragments to GPU KV cache.
- Paper B (attention-sparse cross-attend): suggests cross-attention to a compact memory bank instead of concatenation. Promising for cost but harder to do with standard causal decoding flow.

Practical heuristics to try (ordered by cheap->expensive):
1) Sliding-window dense score + freshness boost: score fragment by (bi-encoder similarity to prompt) + lambda * recency. Tune lambda on dev set. Cheap: encoder on CPU, batched.
2) Lightweight lexical beacon markers: detect named entities + anchors (dates, policy IDs) and always include fragments with anchors matching current query.
3) Two-phase selection: lexical filter (fast) -> bi-encoder rerank top 50 -> cross-check with a tiny, finetuned ranker (distil-BERT) for final top 8.
4) Incremental KV warm-start: keep KV shards for last N turns; on a selection change, only inject diffs to runtime. Need support in Redwood runtime for patching KV without full reload (ask infra/sre).

Experiment matrix (dev cluster):
- Dataset: synthetic-long-chatset-v3 (1000 sessions), plus small sample from customer-beta-3 (anonymized).
- Metrics: token generation P95 latency, top-K recall of referenced ground-truth passages (R@1,R@3), hallucination rate on targeted prompts (qual/auto), and cost delta per 1k requests.
- Config dims: chunk size (256/512/1024 tokens), selection budget (K=4/8/12), freshness lambda (0.0/0.5/1.0), encoder type (tfidf/bi-encoder-small/bi-encoder-medium).
- Runtime knobs: batching window (5/20ms), allow KV patching (true/false), quantization for encoder (int8 vs fp16).

Early micro-probe (ran 2027-11-05):
- Setup: chunk=512, K=8, encoder=mini-simcse (cpu), freshness=0.5.
- Result: P95 down 35% vs naively concatenating whole 8k tokens; R@3 drop ~6% on synthetic set. Qual: model preserved policy lines more often, lost some tangential context. Cost: encoder CPU overhead ~+0.8ms per request (batched), acceptable.
- Takeaway: selection works; biggest win when combined with incremental KV patching.

Open engineering questions / blockers:
- Runtime: can we patch KV cache incrementally? If not, swapping full KV is heavy. Action: ping infra/serving runtime (Arjun) to surface API/limits. Linked ticket: JIRA:INFER-8421.
- Consistency: how to keep KV versions per user session without exploding memory? Idea: LRU of session shards with TTL + fallback to disk-backed cold store (S3) + lazy load. Need SRE input on eviction thresholds and effect on latency.
- Eval sensitivity: current automatic hallucination metric is noisy over short prompts. Consider manual annotation for 200 sessions to calibrate.

Short-term next steps (1–2 sprints):
- Sprint 1: implement prototype selection pipeline (tf-idf + mini-encoder rerank), run baseline matrix, record latency and recall. Owner: Sasha + Arjun.
- Sprint 2: prototype KV diff/patch experiment on dev infra; if not possible, emulate by precomputing partial KV states and measuring swap cost. Owner: Arjun + infra.
- Sprint 3: small human eval of hallucination/recall on customer-like prompts. Owner: Maya.

Rough TODO list (in-notebook):
- [ ] Add short unit tests for chunking logic (edge cases: overlapping anchors, very short fragments).
- [ ] Add flags to selection pipeline for freshness weight and hard anchor inclusion.
- [ ] Wire telemetry: per-request selection size, avg encoder time, KV patch latency.
- [ ] Prepare short demo for product (show latency/relevance tradeoffs).

Open hypothesis (for validation):
- H1: For conversational product workloads, a K=6 selection with freshness boost recovers >=95% of downstream QA recall while reducing P95 latency by ~30% relative to full concat.
- H2: Incremental KV patching yields >2x better latency/cost tradeoff than full KV swaps for sessions longer than 10 turns.

Random notes & heuristics (brain-only):
- Anchor bias: when anchors match, favor earlier fragment (stability) vs always latest (recency) — test both.
- Mixed modality future: for docs with images, precompute visual anchors and treat them as high-precision anchors.
- Consider tiny \"context-sampler\" RL objective later: reward downstream answer correctness given selection budget. Too ambitious for now.

References to re-read next week:
- dense retrieval + rerank primer (arXiv:2306.16560)
- cross-attend memory approaches (internal slides: CONF:inference/memory-bank-2027)
- Redwood runtime notes on KV patching (internal repo PR above)

Notes-to-self end. Keep this lightweight; will convert into proper PRD if micro-probe results look promising.

Sasha
